doc.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Musical parents: singer Sandy Stewart and her hit My Coloring Book
summary: He grew up naturally with music; his mother Sandy Stewart sang with Benny Goodman, on TV shows, and had a Grammy-nominated hit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you get a music education in the college level?
Well I grew up very naturally with music, because both of my parents are musicians.
Your mother was a singer, is that right?

Still is. Sandy Stewart. And a great singer who sang with Benny Goodman and was a regular on the Perry Como Show, the Mitch Miller Show, things like that. She had something of a hit record, a minor hit at least in the 60’s, a song called “My Coloring Book,” which was Kander & Ebb’s first hit, the writers Kander and Ebb. And she was nominated for a Grammy. So she’s a professional singer, a great one. Ella Fitzgerald won that year, and she was pretty good. So.

Yes, she was. She is a marvelous singer. And my father was [Mark] Moose Charlap who was a songwriter/composer. The most famous thing he’s known for is the music from “Peter Pan,” — Mary Martin Peter Pan, which he wrote most of the music for — songs
